text:
incident-bot: ALERT fired: latency.p99 > 1200ms on service=redwood-runtime-prod region=us-west-2 (alert_id=alert-7f3a). Auto-threshold: p99_tail. Link: https://alerts.redwood.internal/alerts/alert-7f3a :rotating_light:

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty incident created: PD-98231. Escalation policy: oncall-sre. Triggered by: alert-7f3a. Pager link: https://pd.redwood.internal/incidents/PD-98231

sre-oncall: acking PD-98231. I'm on it. Quick check: is this global or single-region?

mila: seeing spike in us-west-2 only. p95 ~ 450ms, p99 ~ 1.3s for text-generation route. Metrics: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/latency/runtime?orgId=1&var-region=us-west-2

alicia: confirming — sudden jump ~09:02 UTC, coincides with a burst of large-context requests from a single customer org (org_id=acme-42). Their median token length shot up.

tom: possible kv-cache churn. Logs show repeated cold cache misses to KV shard kvc-13. Patchy cache retention after eviction flood.

infra-eng: running quick check on node health and GPU memory:
```
# ssh to pool
kubectl get pods -n runtime -l app=redwood-runtime -o wide
kubectl top pod -n runtime | grep gpu
```
Seeing 3/12 nodes with GPU memory > 90%. Also noticed sidecar backpressure logs: `sidecar: max inflight exceeded, rejecting`.

sre-oncall: timeline: alert at 09:02, page at 09:03, ack at 09:04. Mitigation attempts: 1) route heavy customers to dedicated pool 2) enable short-circuit fallback to quantized-v2 model 3) temporarily increase per-route concurrency cap. Which to try first?

mila: recommend route heavy org to dedicated pool (dedicated capacity available in us-west-2 spare). That avoids global impact and buys time to warm KV caches.

alicia: raising a temporary routing rule now: `route.match(org_id=acme-42) -> pool=dedicated-east-burst` (will test dry-run then flip).

pagerduty-bot: PD-98231: escalation notification sent to oncall-rotation. No escalation needed, incident is acknowledged.

infra-eng: applying routing change (dry-run) -> success. Flipping to active in 30s.

sre-oncall: flipping now. Watch p99.

mila: p99 dropping to ~780ms within 45s of the route cutover. p95 stable ~420ms. Still seeing some hotkeys in kvc-13 from other orgs, but impact mostly isolated.

ops-lead: customer impact? Any production-facing dashboards or customers complaining? Any SLO breaches for paid customers?

alicia: acme-42 saw 80%+ increased error latency (timeouts at 10s for a handful of requests) during the initial burst. We have one support ticket and a customer message in the console. No broad customer-facing alerts.

tom: follow-up: other nodes still have hot GC/sidecar rejections. Recommend scaling targeted pool by +2 GPUs to offload remaining in-flight long-context work.

infra-eng: scaling dedicated-east-burst pool +2 gpus now. Command: `infractl pool scale dedicated-east-burst --add-gpus 2 --region us-west-2 --reason "latency burst acme-42"`

incident-bot: Action logged: routing rule applied, pool scaled.

mila: after scale, p99 ~ 410ms for routed traffic. Global p99 ~ 460ms. Looks stable. KV miss rate dropping.

sre-oncall: good. Add note: disable autoscaler scale-in for 15m to avoid churn. Also create a short-lived alert suppression to avoid repeated pages while we monitor:
```
# suppression
alerts.suppress(alert_id=alert-7f3a, duration=15m, reason="mitigating via routing+scale")
```

pagerduty-bot: PD-98231 status: acknowledged -> resolved by user action? (manual resolve required).

ops-lead: next steps: post-incident analysis, determine if KV eviction policy needs tuning, examine customer's request patterns (we saw a batch of 150 concurrent long-context calls), and add a guardrail (token length limit or warn on heavy patterns).

alicia: creating a follow-up ticket on backlog: TKT-5512 (investigate KV eviction pressure + routing guardrails). Assigning to infra-eng + runtime-team.

sre-oncall: preparing handoff to next oncall. Summary: quick routing change + +2 GPU scale solved p99 spike. Customer acme-42 experienced elevated latency and a support ticket. No widespread customer outages. Suppression active for 15m. Handoff to next-oncall in 10m.

next-oncall: received. I'll monitor the suppression window and ensure scale remains. If p99 creeps back above 900ms, I'll reopen PD and escalate.

incident-bot: Thread closed for now. Incident summary will be posted to #incidents within the hour.

[reactions: :thumbsup: from alicia, :white_check_mark: from mila]
